cohort: Pregnant women with early-onset and late-onset preeclampsia
finding: Women with early-onset preeclampsia had higher rates of adverse maternal and perinatal outcomes, including C-section, placental abruption, HELLP syndrome, disseminated intravascular coagulation, stillbirths, fetal growth restriction, abnormal Apgar scores, NICU admissions, neonatal death, and placental pathological changes compared to those with late-onset preeclampsia.
mod_finding: C-section rate was higher in the early-onset preeclampsia group.
gest_age: Varied, study compared early and late onset preeclampsia
